glossary.definition: RLHF is the technique AI labs use to make a raw, freshly-trained language model actually behave helpfully and safely. Human reviewers look at pairs of AI responses to the same question and pick the better one, and the model is retrained to produce more answers like the ones humans preferred. Think of it as a talented but very literal new employee, submitted their first drafts to an editor over and over until their instincts started matching what people actually wanted. It's a major reason today's chatbots feel conversational and considerate rather than just spitting out raw predicted text.

items.title: Intel, Broadcom CEOs flag AI industry challenges at financial event
items.summary: Intel Corp. , have flagged capital access as a potential challenge for the artificial intelligence sector. The executives shared their observations today during a financial conference in Singapore. Intel and Broadcom are two of the AI industry’s most important chip suppliers. The former company’s central processing units are in high demand because AI agents need them to run their tools.

items.title: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
items.summary: Epic Games is shifting to an "AI first" development strategy for its collaboration with the Walt Disney Company, letting AI models write all the code and guide all the artwork for an upcoming shooter. That's according to a Bloomberg report , which cites unnamed people familiar with the project who commented on the significant pivot in internal development at the Unreal Engine maker. Human developers will be tasked with managing and guiding code and art assets generated by models such as Anthropic's Claude, according to internal Epic employee messages viewed by Bloomberg. That means "no more hand-written code" and art assets "generated with full AI workflows," according to the report.

items.title: Humanoid bottlenecks emerge amid US-China tensions
items.summary: -China tensions could make it harder for Western manufacturers to secure alternatives to Chinese suppliers.

items.title: Sakana AI's self-improving model gets better at solving and judging, but can't catch its own blind spots
items.summary: Sakana AI's MASS method lets one language model improve itself by solving tasks, judging results, and refining workflows, reaching a win rate of nearly 70 percent against the base model after two rounds. But when the model misses the same errors across all three roles, it can mistake them for progress and reinforce them during training. The study finds gains across all three roles, but shared blind spots can let errors pass as progress and feed into the next training cycle. Researchers from Sakana AI and UC Berkeley have introduced "Multi-Agent Self-Supervision" (MASS), a method for recursive self-improvement (RSI).

items.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
items.summary: Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding. Meta’s Superintelligence Lab released a pair of new state-of-the-art models on Monday, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, representing the company’s first attempt at a frontier model. According to Meta’s testing (presented in the model card ), Wonder and Wonder Full achieve comparable benchmark scores to Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. “Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” Meta’s blog post about the models reads.

items.title: Elon Musk Bragged About His Grok Lego Star Wars Haul. Then X Users Punked Him
items.summary: Musk, we find your lack of security disturbing. There's been a disturbance in the force. Only it's more like a farce. It seems that Elon Musk, while crowing on X about how useful his Grok Bot AI agent was in ordering some Lego Star Wars kits on Sunday, managed to reveal via a screenshot to his more than 240 million followers not only the 10-digit Lego order number of his purchase, but also what he paid for the sets, the delivery and billing addresses, the last four digits of his credit card, and the email address his bot used to buy the bricks from Lego .

items.title: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
items.summary: S. military contract worth almost $50 million. Air Force will buy data collected by WindBorne Systems ‘ fleet of autonomous weather balloons under a new contract that could be worth nearly $50 million to the startup. WindBorne currently has about 700 weather balloons flying around the globe, collecting atmospheric sensor readings that the company sells to customers and also feeds into its own AI weather forecasting model.

items.title: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
items.summary: Meta is making up for lost time in the AI race. After launching Muse Spark , the first model from its revamped Superintelligence Labs division, and buzzy AI agent Muse , it's now launching two new models it claims can go toe-to-toe with the industry's best. The new models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, are available for Muse Code subscribers starting today. Wonder can also be accessed through the Meta Model API, Meta said.

items.title: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs
items.summary: Microsoft is announcing its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip today, designed to be the "primary AI inference system" for Microsoft's products and services. Maia 300 not only improves the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud, it's also more capable of handling the latest reasoning models and agentic tasks. Maia 300 will start being rolled out to production in 2027, and it has been designed with efficiency in mind. "We expect Maia 300 to deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt compared to leading GPU-based systems," says Scott Guthrie , executive vice president of Microsoft's cloud group.

items.title: Prompt: AI agents are running into the limits of access
items.summary: As agents take on more work for users, companies are deciding whether to let outside AI systems act on their platforms.
